extracted.intended_audience: politically engaged British public and readers of political pamphlets (late-18th-century), critics of the French Revolution
extracted.subtask_description: A conservative political essay arguing against revolutionary change in favour of prudence, experience, and constitutional complexity; addresses how governments, rights, and public sentiment should be judged and conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for experience and established institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extraordinary caution before pulling down an edifice which has answered in any tolerable degree for ages the common purposes of society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The science of government is practical and requires more experience than any single person can gain; therefore one ought to exercise 'infinite caution' in overturning long-standing institutions. Anti-pattern: dismantling institutions on purely abstract grounds or short theoretical arguments without models of approved utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject metaphysical/abstract rights as sole political guide
rubrics_metrics.description: The pretended rights of theorists are extremes; metaphysically true may be morally and politically false — rights of men in government occupy a middle ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political arrangements should not be based on abstract perfection of natural rights. Instead, recognise that rights in society are compromises and balances. Anti-pattern: treating abstract 'rights' as immutable prescriptions that forbid compromise or prescription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil society is founded on convention; powers are creatures of convention
rubrics_metrics.description: If civil society be the offspring of convention, that convention must be its law; legislative, judicial, and executory powers are its creatures and have no being outside it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims to rights or powers that contradict the conventions necessary for civil society are 'absolutely repugnant' to that society. Evaluate institutional claims by reference to the conventions that constitute civil association.

rubrics_metrics.name: No man should be judge in his own cause
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the first motives to civil society and a fundamental rule is that no man should be judge in his own cause; by entering society he abdicates that uncovenanted right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justice requires surrendering certain natural prerogatives (self-judgment, unlimited self-defence) into institutional mechanisms. Criterion for legitimate institutions: they prevent private adjudication of one's own interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government as a contrivance to provide for human wants
rubrics_metrics.description: Government is a contrivance of human wisdom to provide for human wants; men have a right that these wants should be provided for by this wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess governments by how well they provide for collective needs (restraint of passions, administration of justice, provision of means for industry). Avoid treating government as the mere protector of abstract entitlements divorced from utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Count restraints among rights; rights and restrictions vary with circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The restraints on men, as well as their liberties, are to be reckoned among their rights; liberties and restrictions admit of infinite modifications and cannot be settled on abstract rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to fix liberties by universal metaphysical rules; adapt distribution of liberties and restraints to times, circumstances, and practical considerations. Anti-pattern: invoking timeless formulas to settle contingent constitutional arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional design requires complexity and practical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The constitution of a state and the distribution of its powers is a matter of the most delicate and complicated skill; simple governments are fundamentally defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer complicated, pragmatic arrangements that compromise conflicting ends over 'simple' schemes that perfectly answer a single end but neglect others. Criterion: does a proposed constitution address the manifold ends of society rather than a single aim?

rubrics_metrics.name: Political reason is prudential calculation and compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights of men in governments are their advantages; these are often balances between differences of good, compromises sometimes between good and evil, and sometimes between evil and evil. Political reason is a computing principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate policies and institutions in terms of comparative advantages and trade-offs rather than absolute moral categories. Anti-pattern: moralizing politics as if outcomes could be reduced to single mathematical truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish power from right; rights must be reasonable and beneficial
rubrics_metrics.description: By theorists the right of the people is almost always sophistically confounded with their power. Men have no right to what is not reasonable, and to what is not for their benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't equate the ability of a body to act with moral or legal right to act. Assess claims to action by reasonableness and public benefit, not merely by majority power or force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose habitual glorification of resistance and revolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Continual talk of resistance and revolution renders the habit of society dangerously valetudinary; it relaxes and wears out the spirit which is to be exerted on great occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resistance should be exercised sparingly and for genuine necessity; habitual revolutionary rhetoric dulls moral sensibility and undermines effective resistance when truly required. Anti-pattern: treating revolution as a routine remedy or political pastime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward political theorists who prefer spectacle over practical reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who value extreme theories often prefer spectacle, magnificent stage effects, and grand scenes to gradual, moderate, practical improvements; they may abandon principles when theory meets practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate political actors by their willingness to pursue tedious, moderate, practical resistance and reform rather than theatrical or absolutist projects. Beware hypocrisy: theorists may profess radical principles without intending practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemn triumphalism that celebrates violence and atrocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Triumphal celebrations of massacres, assassinations, and confiscations are morally abhorrent; to rejoice in the slaughter of innocents is shocking to civilized sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public commemoration and rhetoric should not sanctify or trivialize violent acts. Anti-pattern: religious or celebratory language used to applaud atrocities or to compare them with sacred events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of deliberative bodies requires independence from coercion and mob influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemblies that deliberate under the dominion of an armed force, or before a riotous gallery, where measures are decided before debate, lack the physiognomy and aspect of a grave legislative body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legislative legitimacy by procedural independence, absence of coercion, and freedom from club/mob pre-decision. Anti-patterns: decisions 'decided before they are debated', influence of clubs, armed coercion over representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetoric of extremism hardens moral sentiments and perverts sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: The politics of revolution temper and harden the breast, preparing it for desperate strokes; the mind receives a gratuitous taint and the moral sentiments suffer when no political purpose is served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cultivating a political culture in which extreme rhetoric normalizes cruelty and inhibits humane sympathies; prefer rhetoric that preserves moral sentiment and compassion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of victims: caution against scornful amnesty or consolations
rubrics_metrics.description: Administering 'the opiate potion of amnesty, powdered with all the ingredients of scorn and contempt' is to force victims to drink 'the cup of human misery full to the brim.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing injured parties, act with genuine compassion and avoid offerings that combine contempt with supposed consolation. Evaluate policies of pardon, amnesty, or reconciliation by their dignity and real alleviation of suffering, not by political expediency or scorn.
